div.div:
Why FULL, not BACKWARD
BACKWARD alone permits field removal: a new reader just ignores the dropped field.
FULL is also what a rolling upgrade needs, where two versions are live at once.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 354px; height: 1px; padding-top: 333px; margin-left: 605px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
One definition, not two
EnrichedTradeEvent embeds TradeEvent, so it registers as a reference to trades.raw-value rather than inlining it.
Inlining would give the registry two definitions of one record.

div.div:
When the gate fails
Allowed: add an optional field with a default, widen a union.
Not allowed: remove or rename a field, change a type, add a mandatory field without a default.
Accept a deliberate break with ./gradlew updateSchemaBaseline, which produces a reviewable diff.
